newsitem.title: MEXICO: Telmex buoys Mexico stocks against Dow undertow.
newsitem.headline: Telmex buoys Mexico stocks against Dow undertow.

text.p: Market bellwether Telefonos de Mexico shored up Mexican stocks for the second day in a row Wednesday and helped the market shrug off the ill-effects of a sluggish New York bourse.

"The market was hauled up at the close by Telmex again. It gained in New York. I don't think it can be anything else, because we're still a bit apathetic here," said a trader from Abaco brokerage firm.
The leading IPC index closed up 15.21 points, or 0.45 percent, to an even 3,369.00
Telmex ADRs gained 1/4 to $33-1/4 in New York, while their L series shares gained 12 centavos (2 cents) to 12.46 ($1.66) pesos in Mexico, a gain of some 0.97 percent.
Aside from Telmex, equity analysts said the bolsa was still marked by low volume and selective demand.

"The bolsa is still waiting for new developments to spur trading in a better direction ... we're waiting for several variables to be cleared up, like the new version of the Alliance for Economic Recovery, to know what we can expect next year," said Esteban Rojas, deputy director of analysis at the Arka brokerage.
Mexican Commerce Minister Herminio Blanco said on Wednesday no date had been set for renewal of the Alliance, the government's economic recovery plan.
Brokers said the market was also cautious due to the upcoming Federal reserve meeting to set U.S. interest rate policy.

The percentage gainers list was headed by conglomerate Sidek A series which gained 17 centavos (2 cents) to 2 pesos (27 cents). Dealers said the stock gained on speculation ahead of an expected plan to restructured the firm's troubled finances.

Second place went to financial group Bital, which gained 30 centavos (4 cents) to 4.50 pesos (60 cents). The group's spokeswoman Blanca del Valle told Reuters that holders of 200 million pesos in debentures will be asked during a meeting on Thursday to convert their debt into stock.
